name: Can't Watch
tagline: It's rarely your fight. That's never once stopped you.
epigraph: In 1968, a non-drinker got himself arrested for one of the spirits in this glass.
language_row: Wren's resonance: ready (v2; reaffirmed on v3 and v4 in r5). Guest text 4-gram clean against every pour (Wren r3–r5). Gendered pronouns in the epigraph and y2–y4 refer to Tai Solarin only. Lint warns whoYouAre runs 196 words (examples ~90–150); left as signed, the room's budget being spent.
sources: Fact card `_studio/fact-cards/tai-solarin-ogogoro.md` (Oxford Companion to Spirits & Cocktails, OGOGORO pdf 1417–1418 and pdf 424; *Lagos Daily Times*, 14 Sept 1968, p. 3, "Solarin Freed of Gin Charge", cited by Oxford's bibliography, not read; PUNCH, Adaorah Oduah, 29 July 2022, used as a guard only; ZODML on his *Daily Times* column). Bottle: Difford's Guide (Pedro's, 40%, unaged, redistilled in Lagos); Artifex Drinks (50 cl, £58.95). Drink: *Cocktail Codex* pp. 14, 65, 71, 84; *The Flavor Matrix* checked and set aside (no palm sap, juniper or toffee entry). Room notes `work/outlaw-hero/`.
names_note: Can't Watch (Wren; all three, r4–r5): the person's fear in two words, without spending the tagline. Also considered: One Rule for Both, Fair's Fair (too close to *Fair Measure*).
open_items: The primary source for the arrest, *Lagos Daily Times*, 14 Sept 1968, p. 3, is cited by Oxford but on no open archive Hester could reach; the story rests on Oxford's sentence plus that headline. A library gap for Robin.

Pedro's Premium Ògógóró (unaged) costs about £3.50 a drink (Artifex £58.95 / 50 cl); no true substitute. Fallback: a branded, unaged West African palm-sap spirit, never an unlabelled one; numbers proved for Pedro's at 40% only.

The ban's dates are contested (Oxford: 1919 treaty, still illegal after 1960, changed in 1968; PUNCH: 1910 to 1960), so the reading gives no start year, and says only that the ban ended the same year, not that he caused it.

Equal halves are the room's choice; the Codex's split bases (p. 71) are unequal. *One Table* (ruler-regular-guy) is also a level 30/30/30 split, owned in Siblings: theirs is two sides at the same weight, ours one rule for a local spirit and a foreign one.
Kept out: the *Vanguard* police-station version (wrong date), "risked prison", the day he was freed, naming the law, his school, his other arrests and beliefs, Robin Hood imagery, methanol.
